detail: [XT] quadchk demonstration data for the Gauss-Hermite quadrature check after xtprobit; documented (Stata manual, web-confirmed) as simulated and 'not to be used for analysis'. The x1=-1 / x2 stepping-by-0.05 grid is a designed artefact.
[XT] quadchk demonstration data (the unstable-quadrature companion of quad1) for xtprobit; documented as simulated, not for analysis.

Arellano & Bond (1991) UK firm employment panel; the canonical dynamic-panel GMM example (xtabond/xtdpd/xtdpdsys). Per the [XT] pointer a dynamic-panel example with no random-effects fit is excluded; nL1/nL2/wL1/... are the lagged regressors, yr dummies the period effects. The panel id is a cluster but the manual documents no random effect.

Stata label 'Fictitious cointegration data'; the [XT] xtcointtest (panel cointegration test) example. Made-up data; also a cointegration example (no random-effects fit). RULE GAP: treated 'fictitious' as equivalent to 'simulated'.

[XT] xtdescribe example illustrating gappy/unbalanced panel structure (patient, time, x). x carries no variable label and no documented model; the dataset exists to demonstrate xtdescribe, not to be modelled. RULE GAP: there is a grouping (patient) and a single measurement x, but x has no defensible documented meaning, so excluded under rule 4 rather than filed RESPONSE INFERRED.

An expanded (1600-row, 400-airline) companion of airacc with explicit latent columns u (per-row unobserved component) and lnpm (=ln pmiles); it is not the documented xtnbreg example (that is airacc, 80 rows). RULE GAP: the help page states nothing; the simulated call rests on the generated u column and the non-appearance in any read example. Could alternatively be 'derived or duplicated table'.

Hausman-Taylor demonstration data generated with explicit component columns: ui (the panel random effect), eit (the idiosyncratic error), z0-z2 (time-invariant regressors) and yit the generated outcome. The real Hausman-Taylor example is psidextract. RULE GAP: inferred simulated from the explicit ui/eit generator columns rather than a stated label.
As xthtaylor1 (adds x1c/x1cb): generated Hausman-Taylor demo data with explicit ui (panel effect) and eit (error) columns. RULE GAP: inferred simulated from the generator columns.
Stata label 'Simulated data of calories consumed for 365 days'; the [XT] xtline (time-series graphing) example with three persons (Tess/Sam/Arnold). Explicitly simulated.

Stata label 'Fictional employment status data'; the [XT] xtologit random-effects ordered-logit example (estatus in {Out of labor force, Unemployed, Employed} per id over years). RULE GAP: treated 'fictional' as 'simulated'; otherwise it would be an ordinal RE row estatus ~ hhchild + hhincome + hhsigno + bwinner + age + (1|id).

[XT] xtprobit example (read from xtprobit.pdf), which states '(synthetic) data on whether workers complain to managers at fast-food restaurants': xtprobit complain age grade south tenure gender race income genderm burger chicken, re; grouping restaurant (workers within restaurant). RULE GAP: treated 'synthetic' as 'simulated'; otherwise a binary RE row with grouping restaurant.

Penn World Table real exchange rates, balanced panel of 151 countries x 34 years; the [XT] xtunitroot panel unit-root example (lnrxrate series, Levin-Lin-Chu etc.). A unit-root test, no random-effects fit; per the [XT] pointer the country panel is a cluster but no random effect is documented.

Dahlberg & Johansson (2000) Swedish municipality fiscal panel (265 municipalities x 9 years); a dynamic-panel / panel-VAR example (expenditures-revenues-grants dynamics via GMM/xtvar). Per the [XT] pointer a dynamic-panel example with no random-effects fit is excluded. Real data, but no RE model documented.

[XT] xtheckman example (read from xtheckman.pdf), which states 'fictional data on 600 adults observed from 2013 to 2016': xtheckman wage c.age##c.age tenure, select(working = c.age##c.age market); wage observed only when working. RULE GAP: treated 'fictional' as 'simulated'; otherwise a selection/RE row wage ~ age + tenure + (1|personid) with working the selection indicator.

The Grunfeld investment data (10 firms x 10 years, invest/market/stock); the [XT] xtgls / xtpcse / sureg FGLS-and-SUR example, which fits pooled models with panel-correlated errors and no random effect. RULE GAP: same underlying data as grunfeld.dta, whose random-coefficients (xtrc) fit is filed in the registry; excluded here because its own documented models carry no random effect, per the [XT] pointer. Alex may prefer to fold it into the grunfeld row instead.
